sentences.en: of DreaMs. So I'll start off, I think, a simple question with probably a long answer, but why do we dream?

sentences.en: Personally, I think that we have rapid eye movement sleep, which is the stage in which most dreams occur, along with all mammals, for a lot of reasons, many

sentences.en: And I think for humans, there's a lot of problem solving that goes on in that state.

sentences.en: But that's my answer.

sentences.en: But that's my, that's my concept of it.

sentences.zh: 嗯，弗洛伊德谈到了日间残留物，这是他的概念之一，至今仍被相当严肃地对待。

sentences.en: The idea that, that things that happen in the preceding
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，在前

sentences.en: 18 hours are much likelier to show up in your, your dream than sort of other random previous days.
sentences.zh: 18 小时内发生的事情比其他随机的以前的日子更有可能出现在你的梦里。

sentences.en: And so lots of, lots of dreams are about very recent events and they may be one-time concerns about, about things that just happened that day.
sentences.zh: 所以很多很多的梦都是关于最近发生的事件，它们可能是关于刚刚发生在那天的事情的一次性关切。

sentences.en: Um, and you know, and they're still worth interpreting, but they're going to be about a very specific current sort of issue.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，它们仍然值得解释，但它们将是关于一个非常具体的当前问题。

sentences.en: Whereas if a dream recurs over and over it, I mean, it may be activated by events of a particular day may make a long-term
sentences.zh: 而如果一个梦一遍又一遍地重复，我的意思是，它可能是由特定一天的事件激活的，可能会使一个长期

sentences.en: issue more salient, but it's certainly going to be about something that's a kind of long-term character logic issue for that person.
sentences.zh: 问题更加突出，但它肯定关乎对那个人来说某种长期性格特征的问题。

sentences.en: So in general, we think of recurring dreams as somewhat more important.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，我们认为重复的梦稍微更重要一些。

sentences.en: If you only have time to analyze a few dreams, your recurring dreams would be ones to target.
sentences.zh: 如果你只有时间分析几个梦，你的重复梦将是值得作为目标的。

sentences.en: And often people talk about having nightmares or violent dreaMs. And I've,
sentences.zh: 人们经常谈论做噩梦或极端的梦。而我，

sentences.en: I've spoken to friends and, and, you know, I've myself included, we've had those kinds of scary dreaMs. So what do those dreams mean?
sentences.zh: 我跟朋友交谈过，并且，你知道的，包括我自己，我们都做过那种可怕的梦。那么这些梦意味着什么？

sentences.en: And what do you do if you have violent dreams or nightmares often?
sentences.zh: 如果你经常做极端的梦或噩梦，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: Well, there are two very different kinds.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有两种非常不同的类型。

sentences.en: Um, one is the metaphoric they're, they're scary, but otherwise the content seems much like other dreaMs. It's fairly metaphoric, which is chasing
sentences.zh: 嗯，一种是隐喻性的，它们很吓人，但除此之外内容看起来很像其他梦。它是相当隐喻的，比如在老建筑的走廊里

sentences.en: you down a hall in an old building or something.
sentences.zh: 追你之类的。

sentences.en: Um, and children have more of those kind of garden variety metaphor nightmares than adults.
sentences.zh: 嗯，小孩子比成年人有更多这种大众化的隐喻噩梦。

sentences.en: They tend to decrease with age, but almost everyone has a few of those, um, versus post-traumatic nightmares where you've suffered one or more extremely violent,
sentences.zh: 它们往往随着年龄增长而减少，但几乎每个人都有几个，嗯，相比之下，如果你遭受了一次或多次极度残暴的创伤后噩梦，

sentences.en: terrifying waking life events.
sentences.zh: 恐怖的清醒生活事件。

sentences.en: And in post-traumatic nightmares, the event tends to unfold very much like it did awake.
sentences.zh: 而在创伤后噩梦中，事件的发展往往非常像它醒着的时候一样。

sentences.en: Some people, it replays exactly like they were in a video of, of the episode of getting raped or being in this battlefield or house burning down around them over and over and over
sentences.zh: 有些人，它完全像他们在一个视频里一样重演，关于被强奸或身处这个战场或房子在他们周围烧毁的情节，一遍又一遍，

sentences.en: exactly like it happened.
sentences.zh: 完全就像它发生的那样。

sentences.en: Or more commonly, it's pretty close to how it happened, but it's either got a bit of bizarre dream distortion, but not, not as much as most dreams or often the post-traumatic
sentences.zh: 或者更常见的是，它非常接近它发生的方式，但它要么有一点诡异的梦境扭曲，但没有，不像大多数梦那么多，或者通常是创伤后

sentences.en: nightmares go one step further.
sentences.zh: 噩梦更进一步。

sentences.en: Like somebody was holding a gun to someone's head and threatening to pull the trigger in real life.
sentences.zh: 就像现实生活中有人把枪指着某人的头并威胁要扣动扳机一样。

sentences.en: And they actually do pull the trigger in the, the dream, like the dream goes one step further, whatever was most feared is about to happen actually happens.
sentences.zh: 而他们在梦中真的扣动了扳机，就像梦更进一步一样，最害怕的事情即将发生却真的发生了。

sentences.en: So garden variety nightmares, um, they're, they're just normal to a certain extent.
sentences.zh: 所以普通种类的噩梦，嗯，在某种程度上它们只是正常的。

sentences.en: And some people who have them don't particularly mind them.
sentences.zh: 而且有些做这种梦的人并不特别介意它们。

sentences.en: I've heard a lot of people, um, either say that it's kind of like horror films that, you know, there's a kind of adrenaline rush and they, they kind of enjoy their nightmares.
sentences.zh: 我听到很多人，嗯，要么说这有点像恐怖电影，你知道，有一种肾上腺素激增的感觉，他们，他们某种程度上享受他们的噩梦。

sentences.en: And I've heard other people who say they don't enjoy them, but they feel like they learn something, like it's always pointing out to them things they're anxious about that they
sentences.zh: 我也听到其他人说他们不喜欢，但他们觉得自己学到了一些东西，就像它一直在向他们指出他们焦虑的那些

sentences.en: hadn't thought of.
sentences.zh: 他们没想到的事情。

sentences.en: So many people who have nightmares of, of that kind of garden variety type don't particularly want them to go away.
sentences.zh: 所以许多做那种大众化噩梦的人并不是特别希望它们消失。

sentences.en: And I think that interpreting them just like you would other dreams thinking about, you know, what in my waking life, you know, feels like that feeling and
sentences.zh: 我认为对它们进行解释就像你对待其他梦一样，思考，你知道，我清醒生活中的什么，你知道，感觉就像那种感觉，当女巫在走廊里追我时

sentences.en: the pit of my stomach when the witch is chasing me down the hall is, is, you know, the way to, to deal with those, but post-traumatic nightmares just trauma, re-traumatize people.
sentences.zh: 我胃里翻江倒海的感觉，就是，你知道，处理这些问题的方法，但创伤后噩梦只会让创伤，再次创伤人们。

sentences.en: It's like having the horrible event happening again, night after night, after night, so that it never recedes
sentences.zh: 这就像可怕的事情再次发生，日复一日，夜复一夜，以至于它从未消退

sentences.en: into the paSt. And, and everyone has post-traumatic nightmares, hates having them.
sentences.zh: 进入过去。而且，每个人都有创伤后噩梦，讨厌做这些梦。

sentences.en: Nobody likes those.
sentences.zh: 没有人喜欢那些。

sentences.en: And, and I think that it's also not a mystery.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为这也不是什么谜团。

sentences.en: You know, if you were raped and you're dreaming about a rape or your house burned down and you're dreaming about flames every night, there's not a, gee, why are you dreaming that?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你被强奸了，你梦见被强奸，或者你的房子被烧毁了，你每天晚上都梦见火焰，没有什么“天哪，你为什么做那个梦”的疑问，

sentences.en: Like there is about the witch.
sentences.zh: 就像对女巫的疑问那样。

sentences.en: So there are techniques that can make people stop having post-traumatic nightmares that, um, that involve, you can coach people to just
sentences.zh: 所以有一些技术可以让人停止做创伤后噩梦，嗯，其中包括，你可以指导人们只要

sentences.en: wake up if they start, but it seems to be even more effective to have people come up with an alternate scenario.
sentences.zh: 开始就醒来，但让人想出一个替代方案似乎更有效。

sentences.en: Um, a kind of mastery dream.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一种掌控梦。

sentences.en: If, if the nightmare starts again, how would you like it to come out differently?
sentences.zh: 如果，如果噩梦再次开始，你希望它有怎样不同的结局？

sentences.en: Um, and psychologists kind of happened onto this technique because it happens occasionally, spontaneously.
sentences.zh: 嗯，心理学家偶然发现了这种技术，因为偶尔会自发发生。

sentences.en: People have had a nightmare over and over and over about a real event.
sentences.zh: 人们一遍又一遍地做着关于真实事件的噩梦。

sentences.en: All of a sudden we'll have this dream where someone comes and rescues them, or they are very dreamlike magical way.
sentences.zh: 突然间就会做这样一个梦：有人来救他们，或者他们以非常梦幻般的魔法方式。

sentences.en: The, the whole trauma is swept away and they wake up feeling so much better.
sentences.zh: 整个创伤被一扫而空，他们醒来时感觉好多了。

sentences.en: And so, uh, we found that some people in PTSD groups would hear somebody say, Oh, I used to have a nightmare until one night I had this, this other wonderful dream.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，我们发现 PTSD 群体中的一些人会听到有人说，哦，我以前总做噩梦，直到有一天我做了这个，另一个美妙的梦。

sentences.en: And, and just hearing that the next week, a couple other patients in the group would say they had.
sentences.zh: 而且，仅仅听到这个，第二周，组里的另外几个患者就会说他们也做了。

sentences.en: So now we coach people to come up with an alternate scenario that they would like to see happen and, and kind of get an individual.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们指导人们想出一个他们希望发生并实现的替代方案，并且针对个人。

sentences.en: I mean, for the same sounding trauma, some people would rather have someone rescue them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于听起来相同的创伤，有些人宁愿有人来救他们。

sentences.en: Other people would, would rather like fight off some attacker themselves.
sentences.zh: 其他人，宁愿自己击退袭击者。

sentences.en: A lot of sexual abuse survivors would most like to tell off the abuser about why this was so wrong.
sentences.zh: 许多性虐待幸存者最想做的是向施虐者斥责为什么这大错特错。

sentences.en: Um, and, and other people want very magical, you know, shrink the attacker or the fire down, you know, to a quarter inch high, um, dreamlike things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有其他人想要非常神奇的，你知道的，把袭击者或火缩得只有四分之一英寸高，嗯，梦幻般的事情。

sentences.en: So once you come up with an alternate scenario, you practice that at bedtime.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你想出了一个替代方案，你在睡前练习它。

sentences.en: This is again, another variation on dream incubation, just telling yourself, you know,
sentences.zh: 这又是梦境孵化的另一种变体，只是告诉自己，你知道的，

sentences.en: if my traumatic nightmare starts, I, you know, I want, you know, this scenario and picture the alternate scenario.
sentences.zh: 如果我的创伤性噩梦开始，我，你知道，我想要，你知道，这个方案并想象那个替代方案。

sentences.en: And, and that, that works for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 而且，这，这对很多人都有效。

sentences.en: A lot of people have the alternate dream and then never have the nightmare again.
sentences.zh: 很多人做了替代梦，然后就再也没有做过噩梦。

sentences.en: And then in the research studies, some people do that and the nightmares stop without their, at least consciously recalling, uh, having the alternate
sentences.zh: 然后在这项研究中，有些人这样做了，噩梦就停止了，而他们至少没有有意识地回忆起，呃，做过那个替代

sentences.en: dreaMs. So we don't really know if they have it and forget it, but it still serves its purpose or
sentences.zh: 梦。所以我们真的不知道他们是做了并忘记了，但它仍然达到了目的，还是

sentences.en: if simply the visualization of the scenario, you know, awake at bedtime has a similar effect for some people.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是对该方案的可视化，你知道，在睡前清醒时对某些人有类似的效果。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's really fascinating that you have some control over this.
sentences.zh: 你能对此有一些控制，这真的很令人着迷。

sentences.en: I mean, if you tell yourself you want this dream to stop or to reach a better conclusion, that's really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你告诉自己你想让这个梦停止或者达到一个更好的结局，这真的非常迷人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the, the, the areas in our brain associated with memory are not quite as active, but they're certainly, they're certainly somewhat awake as we dream.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们大脑中与记忆相关的区域并没有那么活跃，但当我们做梦时，它们肯定，肯定在一定程度上是醒着的。

sentences.en: So requests to our dreaming mind do very often get through.
sentences.zh: 所以对我们做梦的心灵的请求非常经常能够传达过去。

sentences.en: It's not a one-to-one, you know, just ask for it once and you'll dream on this topic or you'll have this other dream.
sentences.zh: 这不是一一对应的，你知道，只要求一次，你就会在这个主题上做梦或者你会做这个别的梦。

sentences.en: But, but it's, it's very often effective, especially with repetition more than one night.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是它非常经常是有效的，特别是通过不止一个晚上的重复。

sentences.en: And, uh, moving on to, to pets, let's say, I know you said animals, mammals do go into REM sleep, but you know, if you've watched your, your pet dog on the ground,
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，说到宠物，比方说，我知道你说过动物，哺乳动物确实会进入 REM 睡眠，但是，如果你看过你地上的宠物狗，

sentences.en: when their thoughts start falling asleep, my dog barks and she, you know, twitches her legs, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 当它们的思想开始入睡时，我的狗会叫，她，你知道，抽动她的腿，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So it looks like they're dreaming, you know, as far as we can tell, but, um, so do animals dream and how would we know if they do or don't?
sentences.zh: 所以看起来它们确实在做梦，你知道的，就我们所知而言，但是，嗯，动物到底会不会做梦？我们怎么知道它们到底会还是不会？

sentences.en: Um, well, that's a very, that's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的是一个、真的是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Um, I tend to assume that they do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我倾向于认为它们会的。

sentences.en: We know that, that all mammals accept, uh, cetaceans where whales and dolphins do not have REM sleep.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，所有的哺乳动物都——除了鲸鱼和海豚等鲸类没有快速眼动睡眠外——

sentences.en: They have this strange sleep where they with one half of their brain at a time, but all other mammals have alternate between non REM sleep and rapid eye movement sleep.
sentences.zh: 它们有一种奇怪的睡眠方式，一次只让大脑的一半睡觉，但其他所有哺乳动物都在非快速眼动睡眠和快速眼动睡眠之间交替。

sentences.en: And their brain has activity that looks very similar to ours when we are dreaming.
sentences.zh: 而且它们的大脑活动在我们做梦时看起来与我们的非常相似。

sentences.en: So I am willing to make the leap and, and say that I think that mammals are dreaming in whatever their, you know, elephant or mousy or doggy or catty version of, of that is.
sentences.zh: 所以我愿意迈出这一步，说我认为哺乳动物在做属于它们自己的——不管是大象版、老鼠版、狗狗版还是猫猫版的梦。

sentences.en: Some of my colleagues would not, would not say that.
sentences.zh: 我的一些同事可不会这么说。

sentences.en: I mean, that some of my colleagues would not assume any consciousness to other mammalian species or only past a certain level in the evolutionary hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我的一些同事不会认为其他哺乳动物有任何意识，或者只有在进化等级达到某个特定水平之后才有。

sentences.en: Uh, but yeah, I think they, they have the same brain state that we dream in.
sentences.zh: 呃，但是是的，我认为它们、它们拥有我们做梦时相同的脑电状态。

sentences.en: I think they're probably dreaming in some way.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们可能在以某种方式做梦。

sentences.en: The only, the only slight, um, evidence for dream reports from animals,
sentences.zh: 唯一、唯一的轻微证据，关于动物做梦的报告，

sentences.en: um, are, um, Penny Patterson who had the gorillas Coco and Michael, um, Coco died, I believe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是，呃，佩妮·帕特森，她曾养过大猩猩可可和迈克尔，嗯，可可好像已经去世了。

sentences.en: But, um, but Coco used to sign kind of fantastic scenarios right upon awakening and no other time she'd sign
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，但是可可过去常常在刚醒来时打出一些奇妙场景的手势，除此之外别的时候她不会打这种手势——

sentences.en: about cars flying through the sky, or she'd sign something about seeing a person who she actually hadn't seen in six months.
sentences.zh: 关于汽车在空中飞翔，或者关于看到一个她其实已经有六个月没见过的人。

sentences.en: And, and those sort of signing, not real fantastic things only seem to happen upon awakening.
sentences.zh: 而且，这类手势，那些不真实的奇妙事情似乎只发生在刚醒来的时候。

sentences.en: So Penny assumed that those were dream reports and, you know, you could argue about that, but I, you know, I think that sounds quite likely.
sentences.zh: 所以佩妮认为那些就是做梦的报告，你知道的，你可以对此争论不休，但我，你知道的，我觉得这听起来很可能。

sentences.en: And, uh, and the gorilla Michael, who didn't have quite as big a sign vocabulary, uh, but I guess he's still learning.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，大猩猩迈克尔，他的手势词汇量没有那么大，呃，不过我想他还在学习。

sentences.en: He's certainly still alive and well, he was known to have had his entire extended family group killed by poachers.
sentences.zh: 他当然还在世且身体健康，众所周知，他的整个大家庭都被雷霆盗猎者杀害了。

sentences.en: And then he was picked up as an infant and sold through several iterations and eventually,
sentences.zh: 然后他在还是个幼崽时被带走，经过多次转手，最终，

sentences.en: uh, went to Penny's reserve.
sentences.zh: 呃，来到了佩妮的保护区。

sentences.en: So he had a very traumatic killing of all of his family in front of him.
sentences.zh: 所以他经历过所有家人在眼前被残忍杀害的巨大创伤。

sentences.en: Um, and she said that he used to wake up signing bad people, kill gorillas, bad people, kill gorillas.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她说他过去常常醒来时打出“坏人，杀死大猩猩，坏人，杀死大猩猩”的手势。

sentences.en: And again, only in the morning.
sentences.zh: 而且同样地，只在早晨。

sentences.en: So she interpreted that not just as a memory, but as seeming like he was probably having a post-traumatic dream about the event.
sentences.zh: 所以她不仅把这解释为一种记忆，而且看起来他可能是在做关于这件事的创伤后恶梦。

sentences.en: And again, that's, that's, that's very soft evidence.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，那、那、那是非常薄弱的证据。

sentences.en: It's N of two.
sentences.zh: 样本量只有两个。

sentences.en: It's very subjective.
sentences.zh: 这非常主观。

sentences.en: It's fun to think about, but possibly we have dream accounts from two gorillas, but just in general, they, they are having the same brain state as REM sleep.
sentences.zh: 想一想很有趣，虽然我们可能只有两只大猩猩的做梦记录，但总的来说，它们确实拥有与快速眼动睡眠相同的脑电状态。

sentences.en: So I think it's, it's likely that they're dreaming now.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，它们现在在做梦是很有可能的。

sentences.en: They're not necessarily dreaming when they're twitching and moving though, because in humans, although there's something called REM
sentences.zh: 不过，当它们抽搐和移动时，并不一定就是在做梦，因为在人类中，尽管有一种叫做快速眼动睡眠

sentences.en: behavior disorder where you act out your dreams, we are, we, and other mammals are supposed to be paralyzed during REM sleep and normal, healthy people and animals.
sentences.zh: 行为障碍的病症会让你把梦境演出来，但对于正常健康的人和动物来说，在快速眼动睡眠期间我们本该是处于瘫痪状态的。

sentences.en: That is the case where sleepwalking in non REM sleep is much more common for people.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们在非快速眼动睡眠中的梦游要常见得多。

sentences.en: So, um, for a few of them, uh, like one, I dreamed about a mask changing in all these ways.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己，我，我真的很喜欢面具。

sentences.en: I found that I, I, I really love masks.
sentences.zh: 这非常奇妙。

sentences.en: So I take pictures when I go to mask exhibits.
sentences.zh: 所以我去参观面具展时会拍照。

sentences.en: So I already had enough pictures of masks to start morphing into that dream.
sentences.zh: 因此我当时已经有足够多的面具照片，可以开始融合成那个梦境。

sentences.en: But, um, but for the, for the one I just mentioned, I went down, took pictures of the building.
sentences.zh: 但是，嗯，至于刚才提到的那一张，我特地过去拍了那栋建筑物的照片。

sentences.en: And so a real photograph of, of the building was the basic backdrop.
sentences.zh: 所以那栋建筑物真实的摄影照片就成了基础背景。

sentences.en: And I left, I left the sky and the brick in certain areas unchanged so that it kind of looks photographically real.
sentences.zh: 而且我保留了某些区域的天空和砖块不变，这样它看起来在摄影上才显得真实。

sentences.en: But then I, I played somewhat with the surface of the building, but mainly I, I put in little creatures.
sentences.zh: 不过后来我稍微处理了一下建筑物的表面，但主要还是加入了许多小生物。

sentences.en: Um, some of which I created from scratch in digital programs and others.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中有些是我用数码程序从头创作的，还有一些。

sentences.en: I actually took photographs, not of real animals, but of like little carvings of already not quite realistic animals and manipulated them a little bit more digitally.
sentences.zh: 我实际上拍摄的不是真正的动物，而是那些本身就不太真实的动物小雕刻，然后通过数码技术对它们做进一步的处理。

sentences.en: So it's always collaged photography within lots and lots of digital manipulation to give it the surreal look that the dream had.
sentences.zh: 所以这始终是拼贴摄影，其中结合了大量、大量的数码处理，来营造出梦境所具有的超现实感。

sentences.en: So dreams are also an inspiration for you as well.
sentences.zh: 所以梦境对你来说也是一种灵感来源。

sentences.en: Yes, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: I mean, they've been inspiration for, you know, things in my research life and work as a clinician and interpersonal relationships for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，长久以来，它们一直是我的研究生活中各种事物的灵感，也是我作为临床医生开展工作以及人际关系的灵感来源。

sentences.en: And I'd only been writing about art from dreams, but, but lately it's, yeah, all, all of my art is completely inspired by, by dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 以前我只写过关于梦境艺术的文章，但、但最近，是的，我所有的艺术创作完全都是受梦境启发而成的。

sentences.en: Well, that's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for joining us, Dr. Barrett.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您做客我们的节目，巴雷特博士。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Nice to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和您交谈。

sentences.en: If you've been a long time listener or are new to our show, please consider giving us a rating in iTunes, or if you have time, write a review, we'd really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 如果您一直以来都是我们的忠实听众，或者是我们节目的新朋友，请考虑在 iTunes 上给我们打分，如果您有时间的话，写一条评论，我们会非常感激。

sentences.en: Also, we'd like to hear from you directly.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们也希望能直接听到您的声音。

sentences.en: So if you have, if you have any comments about the show or ideas for us, please email me at kluna at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果您对节目有任何意见或建议，请发电子邮件至 kluna@APA.org 联系我。
